finding.summary: setBlockType's switch from a path-range removal to the node-scoped removeNodeStyle has no test
finding.evidence: The diff changes three removal sites from `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` to `removeNodeStyle` and documents the bug being fixed ("on a table block it would also strip `listKind`/`listLevel`/`headingLevel` from every block nested in its cells"). Two of the three sites got dedicated nested-preservation regressions in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts ('should not strip backgroundColor from nodes inside the cell', 'should clear colSpan in the CRDT without touching nested cells'). The setBlockType site (line 1459) got none: the `describe('setBlockType')` block (test file lines 1868-1969) only covers a plain block losing listKind/listLevel and a cell-internal block being retyped — nothing sets a table block's type while nested list-item blocks exist inside its cells, so the exact regression the comment describes would pass unnoticed.

verdict.reason: The setBlockType site (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1459) switched to node-scoped removeNodeStyle with a comment naming the exact regression (a table block stripping listKind/listLevel/headingLevel from blocks nested in its cells), but no test exercises that scenario. Every case in describe('setBlockType') (test lines 1868-1969) uses a plain top-level block, except line 1961-1968 which retypes a cell-INTERNAL block — a case where the old removeStyleByPath(path, path+1) behaves identically, since a cell-internal block's subtree holds only inlines that never carry those attributes. Wider searches found no counterexample: repo-wide grep of all *.test/*.spec files for setBlockType yields only these 8 calls plus the concurrent integration test (line 627-654, plain paragraph, asserts convergence only); the indirect callers (text-style-group.tsx:75, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:591) are tested only with a mocked editor (setBlockType: vi.fn() at color-reset.test.ts:31, toolbar-focus.test.ts:46); packages/docs and packages/slides tests exercise a different in-memory setBlockType; no e2e coverage exists. The two sibling removeNodeStyle sites (2467, 2517) DID get nested-preservation regressions (test lines 2053-2066, 2226-2230), which highlights the gap. Reverting line 1459 would leave the suite green — a clear behavior change with no meaningful test.

finding.summary: Color-reset test cannot distinguish `{ color: undefined }` from `{}` — the exact distinction the fix depends on
finding.evidence: `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` (and the `backgroundColor` twin at line 87) uses jest/vitest recursive equality, which treats an explicitly-`undefined` property as equal to an absent one — `expect({}).toEqual({color: undefined})` passes. The whole point of the change is that the key must be PRESENT with value `undefined`, because the store's clear path keys off `key in style && style[key] === undefined` (see `removedCellStyleAttrs` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:248 and `removedInlineStyleAttrs` at :148). A regression that passed `{}` (key dropped) would leave the stale attribute on the CRDT node and still pass this test. The test does catch the old `""` behavior, so it is not fully vacuous, but it does not cover the property it claims to. A `Object.keys(call[0])` / `'color' in call[0]` assertion would close it.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the test asserts via `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })`, which would be blind to a `{}` regression. That code is not in the repository: a repo-wide grep for `toHaveBeenCalledWith({ (color|backgroundColor)` returns no matches, and the cited line 87 is the opening of the helper `expectClearedOnly`, not an assertion. The actual assertions (color-reset.test.ts:91-97) read the mock call directly and check `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(style, key) === true`, `Object.keys(style)` deep-equals `[key]`, and `style[key]` is undefined. A regression that dropped the key and passed `{}` would fail both the hasOwnProperty assertion and the Object.keys assertion (`[]` vs `['color']`), so the test does distinguish `{ color: undefined }` from `{}` — the exact property the fix depends on per `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (`key in style && style[key] === undefined`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:151). The test's own comment at lines 77-86 documents the vitest recursive-equality pitfall as the reason `toHaveBeenCalledWith` was deliberately avoided. The reviewer's proposed remediation is already implemented verbatim. The file is matched by the vitest `include` globs (vite.config.ts:268), so it is live, not dead code.
